newsitem.title: UK: Brake Bros sees lower-than-expected profit.
newsitem.headline: Brake Bros sees lower-than-expected profit.

text.p: British food supplier Brake Bros Plc said on Monday it expected its net pretax profit for the year to be in the region of 24 million stg, a figure some way below market expectations.
The company had pretax profit of 27.1 million stg last year.
The firm's stock was marked down 178p at 578.5 by 1040 GMT.

The company attributed the shortfall to its multi-temperature distribution business, Puritan Maid Ltd, which it was likely to sustain losses this year of about 4.5 million stg, Brake Bros said in a statement.
The company said top management at the unit had been changed, with Roger Spicer named as managing director, effective from January 1.
Brake Bros said its plans for a 20 million stg development of a distribution centre in Birmingham were well-advanced.
Operations at the site are set to begin early in 1998.
Elsewhere, the company said the performance of its core frozen food division was unchanged from last year.
